facts.statement: Ankistrorhynchus is an extinct genus of sclerorhynchoid fish that lived during the Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: Ankistrorhynchus is an extinct genus of sclerorhynchoid from the Cretaceous Period.

facts.statement: The genus is known only from isolated rostral teeth found in two species.
facts.quote: It is known only isolated rostral teeth from two species.

facts.statement: The species A. lonzeensis was named after its type locality in Lonzée, Belgium.
facts.quote: A. lonzeensis is named for its type locality of Lonzée, Belgium.

facts.statement: The species A. lonzeensis dates to the lower Santonian stage.
facts.quote: It is from the lower Santonian stage.

facts.statement: The species A. washakiensis was described from the Campanian-aged Mesaverde Formation in Wyoming, USA.
facts.quote: A. washakiensis was described from the Campanian-aged Mesaverde Formation of Wyoming, USA.

facts.statement: The species A. major was named from fragmentary material found in New Jersey, USA, making its validity questionable.
facts.quote: The species A. major was named from Campanian/Santonian of New Jersey, USA off of fragmentary material, thus making its validity questionable.

facts.statement: Ankistrorhynchus belongs to the family Sclerorhynchidae.
Ankistrorhynchus is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
The type species of the genus Ankistrorhynchus is A. lonzeensis.
The genus lived from the Santonian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 85.7 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Maastrichtian (85.7 to 66 million years ago)
